status: LOGICAL_OWNER_BOUND_PINNED. The owner terminal-transition bound is 13443 pages, derived from the compiled constants of the pinned SQLite 3.53.4 (modernc.org/sqlite v1.60.1). The gate threshold is 13791 slack pages. Verified in Linux with Go 1.27.1. This covers one reservation followed directly by its terminal write, with no other owner growth in between. It is not physical D14, not protected-root, not WAL, and not host storage.

corrections.what: G1 restated as a tested invariant (gaps_open G1, G2, G5; next_physical_integration 1). The R3 wording called the ungated intervening growth 'material' and 'the largest remaining' gap. In code, while an effect is Reserved, the other owner commits of the same workflow already refuse before any write: AdvanceCheckpoint (recovery.go:878-881), ReservePreEffectRetry (:694), ReserveHostCall (:724, via validateHostCallReservationAdmission :1178-1188), a second ReserveEffect (validateEffectReservationAdmission :1244-1246), and clean restart, which ObserveRecovery refuses (:977, via validateObservedDisposition :2057-2059; validateRestartPins :1692 is a second check). Fresh init of an existing workflow ID returns ErrCAS. TestD14ReservedEffectRefusesNonTerminalCommits pins these refusals and the unchanged head. The residual risks are the root terminal anchor (not gated; its failure poisons the owner after an owner commit, sqlite_linux.go:1112-1124) and another workflow sharing the owner file (not refused by the owner).
corrections.why: The R3 wording overstated an open gap, missed the existing refusals, and did not name the real residual risks.

code_facts: moveToChild returns SQLITE_CORRUPT when iPage >= BTCURSOR_MAX_DEPTH-1 (sqlite_g_000000000001feab.go:10008). A cursor therefore never descends below 20 levels, so each balance chain starts from a tree of at most 20 levels.

balance_nonroot (sqlite_g_000000000001dea8.go:55): apNew [5]uintptr (:61). The sibling count nOld = i+1 is at least 1 (:122). The page count k is capped at NB+2 = 5, with CORRUPT above that (:383). Pages are allocated only for i >= nOld (:529), so one call allocates at most k-nOld <= 4 pages.

balance (sqlite_g_000000000001feab.go:1631-1752): one balance_nonroot or balance_quick per level, going from the leaf toward the root. On root overflow it calls balance_deeper, then balances level 1 once more (:1666-1672).
sqlite3BtreeInsert (sqlite_g_000000000001dea8.go:2043): one _balance call (:2289). sqlite3BtreeDelete has two calls (deab.go:2328, 2340), but no transition deletes.

schema_and_writes.schema: sqlite_linux.go:1204-1247 (was cited as 1189-1230). workflow_recovery_state has a TEXT PRIMARY KEY, which gives one autoindex. workflow_recovery_events has PRIMARY KEY(workflow_id,sequence) and UNIQUE(workflow_id,checkpoint_digest), which give two autoindexes, plus an FK to state and append-only triggers. There are no other indexes. auto_vacuum=NONE is enforced by checkSQLiteFileGeometry, so no pointer-map pages exist.
schema_and_writes.transition_writer: writeNextCheckpoint (sqlite_linux.go:1466) runs one UPDATE of workflow_recovery_state (:1472) and one INSERT into workflow_recovery_events (:1491). The SET list excludes workflow_id, so the state PRIMARY KEY autoindex is unchanged. RecordTerminalEffectOutcome commits once, via l.commit (recovery.go:863). The reservation's gate runs on the same transaction (sqlite_linux.go:1094, inside the block at 1089-1097; was cited as 1079).
schema_and_writes.trees_per_transition: 4, each in one balance chain: state table, events table, events PRIMARY KEY autoindex, events UNIQUE autoindex

bound.usable_page: 4096 bytes. The header reserved-byte count is one u8, so usable >= 3841. The bound uses the 3841 floor, so it holds for any reserved-byte value. The geometry check does not read that byte.

row_overhead_closed_by.state_row_basis: record header 25 (size varint 2 + 5 text serial types 9 + blob serial type 4 + 10 integer types 10) + workflow_id <=256 + 3 digests 192 + deadline <=46 (RFC3339Nano, UTC) + 10 integers <=80
row_overhead_closed_by.event_row_basis: record header 18 + workflow_id 256 + sequence 8 + owner_epoch 8 + expected_digest 64 + checkpoint_digest 64

bound.split_slack_basis: 4 trees x (4*20 + 1). A chain makes at most 20 balance calls of at most 4 pages each, plus 1 page for balance_deeper. After balance_deeper the root gets at most 4 dividers of at most 340 bytes each, far below 3841, so it cannot overflow again within the chain.

Threshold slack = 13791 at zero free pages.

assumptions: A1 verified: BTCURSOR_MAX_DEPTH = 20 and moveToChild enforces it in the compiled pinned source.
A2 verified: balance_nonroot allocates at most 4 pages per call (k <= NB+2 = 5, nOld >= 1).
A3 verified: balance_quick and balance_deeper each allocate exactly one page.
A4 argued from sizes, not measured: after balance_deeper the root holds at most 4 dividers of at most 340 bytes, so at most one balance_deeper per chain.

A5 argued from the SQL shape and the single _balance call in sqlite3BtreeInsert, not traced in VDBE bytecode: each tree gets one chain per transition. The state UPDATE is an overwrite insert and no deletes run.
A6 conservative: freed pages are not credited, and freelist reuse counts as an allocation.
A7 verified in code: page_size=4096, auto_vacuum=NONE, and max_page_count is read on the reservation's connection.

A8 verified in code: workflow_id <= 256 bytes (recovery.go:2206). Blobs <= 16 MiB via schema CHECK (sqlite_linux.go:1217, 1235-1236), maxCheckpointJSONBytes and the encode check (sqlite_linux.go:1509). Deadline is UTC RFC3339Nano (encoded at sqlite_linux.go:1454,1482; UTC normalization at recovery.go:1129,1144,1325), at most 46 bytes.
gaps_open: G1 (closed as a tested invariant on 2026-10-15; this replaces the R3 wording 'material ... not bounded', see corrections): while an effect is Reserved, every other commit of the same workflow is refused before any write with its typed error. AdvanceCheckpoint, ReservePreEffectRetry, ReserveHostCall, and a second ReserveEffect return ErrPendingUnknown; a clean restart cannot be observed, since ObserveRecovery returns ErrPendingUnknown; fresh init of an existing workflow ID returns ErrCAS. TestD14ReservedEffectRefusesNonTerminalCommits pins these refusals and the unchanged head. The reservation-to-terminal window therefore holds only the terminal writes, which the bound covers. A tool call still makes 5 owner commits (TestD14ProductionToolCallCommitsAndEncodedBytes), none of them inside that window. The risks this does not close are named in G2 and G5.

G2: the protected root (4096-page ceiling) is not gated. Its terminal anchor can fail after the owner terminal commit, which poisons the owner (fail-closed, effect unresolved; R2 risk, re-checked 2026-10-15 at sqlite_linux.go:1112-1124). Root fence, epoch, and clock writes (AcquireOwnerEpoch, NextOwnerEpoch, and the clock persisted during verification at protected_root_linux.go:1151) are also not headroom-gated.

G3: the reserved-byte floor costs capacity. Admission ends at page 18977, against 19796 with usable 4096 (terminal 12626 and reservation 346 there), so the floor costs 819 pages, about 3.2 MiB. A minimal refusal of nonzero reserved bytes would recover it, but needs a reserved-byte read path. Not implemented.
G4: physical items remain open: ENOSPC and EDQUOT on the production volume, filesystem overhead, EIO, power loss, and WAL growth (no wal_checkpoint or journal_size_limit, decision 4).

G5: one workflow per owner file is enforced by the catalog (production_workflow_catalog_linux.go:378 builds the path), not by the owner. Another workflow in the same file can consume the reserved headroom without being refused (R2 risk, unchanged, not tested).
G6: the analysis covers only the pinned modernc.org/sqlite v1.60.1. Upgrading it requires re-checking BTCURSOR_MAX_DEPTH, NB, and the allocation counts above.

next_physical_integration: 1. G1 is closed as a tested invariant (see gaps_open). The largest remaining logical risks are the root terminal anchor (G2) and a shared owner file (G5).
2. Bound protected-root terminal growth and reserve it (G2).

3. Physical reserve on the dedicated volume: preallocate the derived owner, root, and audit bound with fsync before ReserveEffect. Release and sync before the protected terminal writes that need the space (Decision 3 of docs/design/d14-reserved-capacity.md). Add crash tests before and after release.
4. Decide the WAL policy (wal_checkpoint or journal_size_limit) and measure filesystem overhead on the production volume (G4).
5. If the 819-page floor cost is unacceptable, add a minimal refusal of nonzero reserved bytes (G3).
